openings.claim: Redistributing the existing surname divider cards to bound smaller, heavily populated surname ranges may shorten shelf searches for correctly filed holds. This evaluates a bounded refinement of parent A; the full pickup target remains unproven.
openings.delta: Keep surname addressing and the same cards, shelves and cart. Change divider positions and range labels so each card accurately identifies its bounded shelf region, concentrating existing cards where surname runs contain more books.
openings.prediction: Among correctly filed shelf holds, retrieval within the first surname region becomes faster after redistribution. Household-name mismatches and cart pickups show little direct improvement; total encounter time may still exceed two minutes during the concentrated arrival interval.
openings.rival_prediction: The nearest alternative explanation is that wrong household surnames and movement between locations dominate delay. It predicts little improvement from sharper divider ranges, with long encounters still concentrated in second-location searches even when the correct shelf region is narrow.
openings.defeat: Matched correctly filed shelf pickups show no reduction in regional search time, or region-search gains leave fewer than 95% of all available-hold encounters within two minutes. Any wrong-reader handoff defeats full-case success; preparation above ten clerk-minutes defeats admissibility.
openings.probe: The existing clerk uses paper, pencils and the timing sheet to record first-region search time, additional searches and total encounter time across comparable evening windows. Reposition existing cards within the remaining ten-minute daily preparation allowance, counting any later preparation corrections against that allowance; stop redistribution when the allowance is exhausted. Keep names and notes behind the desk. Record cart pickups separately without changing their handling.
assumptions: Supplied observations are synthetic stipulations; no improvement has been observed.
The number and distribution of existing divider cards permit useful redistribution; this is unconfirmed.
Accurate relabeling and measurement can fit the preparation allowance; the eight-minute sample does not establish that.
Parent A supplies search boundaries, not verified reader identity or live location tracking. It cannot establish zero wrong-reader handoffs or resolve the full-case queue and location risks.
